newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Nine feared drowned in Colombia river accident.
newsitem.headline: Nine feared drowned in Colombia river accident.

text.p: At least six children and three adults were missing and feared drowned after they were swept away by a raging river in southwest Colombia on Monday, Red Cross officials said.

The group was swimming at a popular bathing spot along the River Jamundi about six miles (10 km) south of Cali, Colombia's second-largest city, when an "avalanche" of rocks and mud washed down the river, Red Cross rescue worker Alberto Catano said.

"It has been raining heavily in the region. First reports say six children and three adults have been washed away by the swollen river. They were bathing at the time," Catano told Reuters by telephone from Cali.
Catano said 25 rescue workers including firefighters, Red Cross volunteers and Civil Defence teams were searching for the missing people.

The River Jamundi rises in the central cordillera of the Andes and flows into the River Cauca, one of the country's largest rivers, about three miles (five km) from where the children and adults were swept away.
